title: Six-class rho on secp256k1: Chebyshev meter control and tightened H1 (126.513)

claims.statement: For uniform full-production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho attack specified in proof.md halts on every run after at most 2^126.513 target-group-operation equivalents: a global meter charges every action before it runs. The ordinary step is not charged as a reference addition plus allowance; it is charged at its counted scalar AArch64 instructions, 860 instructions = 0.860 units of C=1000 (counted 123 + 597 instructions per walk for the two loop passes of kernels/secp_walk.c, clang -O3 -target aarch64-linux-gnu with a nine-instruction inline-assembly modular subtraction, shipped as kernels/secp_loops.s and counted by experiment.py, plus 129 instruction allowances for the class bookkeeping rows, 849 in all); traversal costs 0.890 and doubling at most 2.0, and no reference operation is also charged. Under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random-mapping collision time with slowdown allowance kappa=1.02, floor p0=0.3906 at S_ops/kappa, and a fourth claim that escape counts are 64-dependent sums so that Chebyshev bounds their deviation), the chance of recovery is greater than 0.3905: the meter's early-halt probability is below 2^-75 because W_max covers phase 1, the hard extras and the ceilings of all random charges. The slowdown allowance of H1 is kappa=1.02, supported by a toy census of 162,316 trials (slowdown +1.13% +/- 0.17% at q25, +0.22% +/- 0.20% at q29). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units and included; no nonuniform advice. The walk, class key, canonical-index rule, cycle handling, phases, storage, kernels and bookkeeping rows are those of submission b52f8806 (six-class-rho-secp-counted-v2, 126.60), itself built on a9f1a6fe, 3682292, 758d8df6 and 189ebc42; all are credited dependencies but no prior verdict is a mathematical premise. This is an analytical, heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the field kernels checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, instruction counts parsed from the shipped AArch64 assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
